items.body:
# SPEC — Blocks Event Trigger: workflow node, trigger consumer and Event Triggers page (Phase 2 of 2)

- **Task type:** Feature
- **Target repo:** blocks-logic
- **Repository:** https://github.com/SELISEdigitalplatforms/blocks-logic
- **Implementation scope:** Both. Backend (`server/`) and frontend (`client/`) inside blocks-logic. Function runtime is excluded. The `IsValidForFunction` flag is only shown and edited.
- **External dependencies:** None. Internal dependency: blocks-genesis-net Phase 1 ([SPEC1 (blocks-genesis-net#167)](https://github.com/SELISEdigitalplatforms/blocks-genesis-net/issues/167)), which supplies `BlocksEventTriggerConstants`, `BlocksEventCatalogEntry`, `BlocksEventTriggerMessage` and the producer forwarding. blocks-logic must reference that Genesis version.
- **Ecosystem consideration:** Included. The scope is the Blocks OS internal repositories listed in the blocks-os project skill.
- **Work location:** `C:\Users\Rifat\Documents\Office\Blocks\blocks-logic`.

  Backend paths:
  - `server/Workflow.DomainService/Nodes/TriggerBlocksEventV1/**` (**new**)
  - `server/Workflow.DomainService/BlocksEvents/**` (**new**: catalog service and repository)
  - `server/Workflow.DomainService/Services/WorkflowExecutionService.cs`, `IWorkflowExecutionService.cs`, `WorkflowService.cs`
  - `server/Workflow.DomainService/Repositories/WorkflowRepository.cs`, `IWorkflowRepository.cs`
  - `server/Workflow.DomainService/Utils/Constants.cs`
  - `server/Workflow.DomainService/WorkflowExecutionServiceCollectionExtensions.cs`
  - `server/Worker/Consumers/Workflow/BlocksEventTriggerConsumer.cs` (**new**), `server/Worker/Program.cs`
  - `server/Api/Controllers/BlocksEventTriggerController.cs` (**new**)
  - `server/XUnitTest/**`

  Frontend paths:
  - `client/app/modules/workflow/components/{node-library-panel,node-schemas,node-guides}/**`
  - `client/app/modules/workflow/models/node.model.ts`
  - `client/app/modules/event-triggers/**` (**new**)
  - `client/app/routes/private/event-triggers/event-triggers-page.tsx` (**new**)
  - `client/app/router.tsx` (route only; `client/app/constants/navigation-menus.ts` is **not** changed)
  - `client/app/modules/workflow/components/node-inspector/form-builder/fields/select-field.tsx` and `form-field.types.ts` (add an optional `refetchOnWindowFocus` flag)
  - `server/Directory.Packages.props`: no change needed. `dev` already references `SeliseBlocks.Genesis.OS` `4.5.4`, which contains Phase 1.
  - `e2e/**`
- **GitHub validation:** Ref `dev` @ `2b5cf433ae504bd31c752da68d446182287393fe`. Both layers are present:
  - Backend: `server/Api` (controllers), `server/Worker` (Genesis consumers), `server/Workflow.DomainService`.
  - Frontend: `client/app` (React and Vite routes in `client/app/router.tsx`).

  The local checkout is on `dev` at the same commit, with a clean tree.
- **Board:** Blocks — https://github.com/orgs/SELISEdigitalplatforms/projects/455 (verified 2026-10-28; configured in the skill as "Blocks OS")
- **Planned board status:** Backlog
- **Phase:** Phase 2 of 2. Predecessor: **blocks-genesis-net SPEC1 (Phase 1 of 2)** must be released as a package before this phase can build.

---

## 1. GOAL

This phase lets tenant developers start workflows from Blocks platform events with a new **Blocks Event** trigger node. It also lets project admins choose which events may drive workflows (and, later, functions) on a new **Event Triggers** page.

- The node's dropdown shows only the events enabled for workflows.
- When Genesis forwards an event (Phase 1), every published workflow of that tenant that listens to the event runs, one execution per workflow. This follows the Data Trigger's fan-out.
- **Priority tradeoff:** this phase reuses the Data Trigger's execution path rather than building a new engine path. It runs published workflows only, with no editor test mode, which keeps the change bounded.
- **Success measures (confirmed):**
  - For 1, 10 and 50 matching workflows, the consumer's time from receiving a message to all executions being queued is p95 ≤ the Data Trigger baseline + 10%.
  - The page's list and toggle APIs are p95 ≤ 500 ms with a 200-event catalog.

## 2. USER STORY

- As a **tenant developer** (`blocks-logic::workflow::manage`), I want to add a Blocks Event trigger and pick an enabled event, so that my workflow runs whenever that platform event happens in my project.
- As a **project admin** (`blocks-logic::workflow::manage`), I want to see every catalogued event and switch it on or off for workflows and functions, so that only events I approve can drive automation.
- As a **read-only user** (`blocks-logic::workflow::read`), I want to view the catalog and its flags, so that I know which events are available, without being able to change them.

## 3. CONTEXT

### Purpose
blocks-logic owns workflow orchestration. This phase adds a trigger type and the tenant-facing control over which events Genesis forwards.

### Users and core workflows
- Developers build workflows in the editor (node library, then node inspector) and publish them.
- Published workflows run from triggers: webhook, email, data, schedule, and now Blocks Event.
- Admins manage settings pages in the logic console, which has Schedules, Workflow, Functions and Proxy menus.

### Architecture and ownership
Existing code at `2b5cf433`:
- **Data Trigger fan-out (the reference implementation).** `server/Workflow.DomainService/Services/WorkflowExecutionService.cs`:
  - `DataTriggerStartAsync` (≈ line 930) reads the tenant from `BlocksContext`. It calls `GetPublishWorkflowsByDataCollectionAsync`, resolves each published version snapshot (`_workflowVersionRepository.GetWorkflowVersionsAsync`), and loops over **every** workflow calling `QueueDataTriggerExecutionAsync`.
  - `QueueDataTriggerExecutionAsync` (≈ line 1059) finds the matching trigger node, creates the execution (`CreateExecutionAsync`), sets `Context["Input"]` and `Status=Queued`, and sends `AddExcuationNodeEvent` to `LogicConstants.NodeQueueFor(execution.Id)`. It wraps each workflow in its own `try/catch`, so one failure does not stop the others.

  [source](https://github.com/SELISEdigitalplatforms/blocks-logic/blob/2b5cf433ae504bd31c752da68d446182287393fe/server/Workflow.DomainService/Services/WorkflowExecutionService.cs)
- **Published workflow query.** `server/Workflow.DomainService/Repositories/WorkflowRepository.cs` `GetPublishWorkflowsByDataCollectionAsync` (≈ line 200) filters with `IsPublished == true` plus `ElemMatch(PublishedMeta.TriggerNodes, {Type, Category="trigger", Parameters.*})`, through `ReadAsync` (data-access scope). [source](https://github.com/SELISEdigitalplatforms/blocks-logic/blob/2b5cf433ae504bd31c752da68d446182287393fe/server/Workflow.DomainService/Repositories/WorkflowRepository.cs)
- **Publish.** `server/Workflow.DomainService/Services/WorkflowService.cs` `PublishAsync` and `PublishVersionAsync` (≈ lines 590–760). `CloneTriggerNodes` copies every `Category=="trigger"` node into `PublishedMeta.TriggerNodes`, so the new node is captured with no change.
- **Node executor pattern.** `server/Workflow.DomainService/Nodes/TriggerDataV1/TriggerDataV1Node.cs` (`NodeType="dataGateway"`; it outputs `Input` items on the `source` branch). It is registered in `WorkflowExecutionServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:62`.
- **Worker consumers.**
  - `server/Worker/Program.cs:84` registers `IConsumer<DataChangeEvent>, DataTriggerConsumer`.
  - Queue bindings live in `server/Workflow.DomainService/Utils/Constants.cs`:
    - RabbitMQ `ConsumerSubscriptions`, for example `BindToQueue(DataTriggerQueue,10)` at line 96.
    - Azure `Queues` list at line 121.
- **API conventions.** `server/Api/Controllers/WorkflowController.cs` uses `[Route("[controller]/[action]")]` with `[ProtectedEndPoint("blocks-logic::workflow::read" | "blocks-logic::workflow::manage")]`.
- **Key-value store.** Genesis `IKeyValueStore` (tenant DB `KeyValueStores`, `impersonated: true`), used by logic in `server/CloudConfiguration.DomainService/Shared/Services/ConfigurationRepository.cs`.
- **Client node system:**
  - `client/app/modules/workflow/components/node-library-panel/node-definitions.tsx` (the Data Trigger entry is at line 54).
  - `node-schemas/node-schema-trigger-dataGateway-v1.ts`: a searchable async `select` with an `options` loader, a `display` output block and a `callout-accordion-display` note.
  - `node-schemas/node-schemas.ts:22` maps the schema.
  - `models/node.model.ts:18` holds the type union.
  - `node-guides/node-guide-trigger-dataGateway-v1.tsx`.
- **Client shell.** `client/app/router.tsx` (lines 93–109, the `:itemId` children). The page is a route here, but it is deliberately **not** added to `client/app/constants/navigation-menus.ts`: it is reached only from the Blocks Event node.
- **Select field.** `node-inspector/form-builder/fields/select-field.tsx` loads async `options` once in a `useEffect`, keyed on `optionsDependencies`. It does not reload on its own, so a toggle made in another tab would not show up until the inspector is reopened. This phase adds an opt-in reload when the window regains focus.
- **Genesis package.** `server/Directory.Packages.props` references `SeliseBlocks.Genesis.OS` `4.5.4` (commit `2b5cf433`). That is the NuGet release built from blocks-genesis-net `main` `7325152`. It contains Phase 1, which is PR #174 merged as `5e4575b`, plus the Sonar fix `03a054b`.
  - The csproj still declares `4.6.0`: `release.yml` takes only the major from it, and numbers the release from NuGet.
- **What Phase 1 actually shipped** (blocks-genesis-net#167, decisions Q1–Q8, all option A). Each point differs from, or adds to, SPEC1:
  - **Namespace.** The contracts are `BlocksEventTriggerConstants`, `BlocksEventCatalogEntry` and `BlocksEventTriggerMessage`, in namespace **`Blocks.Genesis`** under `src/Genesis/Message/BlocksEventTrigger/`, so no extra `using` is needed. `BlocksEventCatalogEntry` is `[BsonIgnoreExtraElements]`. Its `SourceServiceKeys` and `ConsumerNames` are `string[]`. It has no `SortOrder`.
  - **Catalog read.** Genesis reads the catalog as a `BsonArray` and maps each element separately: a malformed entry, or one with a non-bool flag, is skipped. This phase's catalog service must read the same way, so one bad element never hides the whole catalog.
  - **Scheduling.** RabbitMQ forwards are never scheduled, and neither are RabbitMQ originals. Azure forwards keep the original's `ScheduledEnqueueTimeUtc`.
  - **Size cap.** `MaxForwardBytes` (196,608) applies to the whole serialized forward envelope, not only the payload.
  - **Azure forwards** use a separate `ServiceBusClient` with no retries.
  - **RabbitMQ returns.** Returned messages are logged without bodies, so a returned forward logs only its `EventName`.
- **Upstream since the first draft.** Between `3bddee91` and `2b5cf433`, blocks-logic gained the Genesis notifications and mobile-push work. `Constants.cs` now also binds `NotificationQueues.Push`. The new Blocks Event queue goes into the same RabbitMQ `ConsumerSubscriptions` list and Azure `Queues` list. The push request, `PushRequested`, is a catalogued event.
- **Upstream since the first draft.** Between `c21f35d4` and `3bddee91`, blocks-logic gained mail and Service Bus secret reads, lint and Sonar cleanups, and a client move to `zod` 4 and `@hookform/resolvers` 5. None of these touch the workflow, worker, trigger or catalog paths in this spec. New client code must use the zod 4 API.
- **Ownership.**
  - Genesis (Phase 1) owns forwarding, the catalog contracts and the cache.
  - This phase owns the catalog writes, the invalidation publish, the consumer, the node and the page.
  - Seeding is a manual operator step: `output/seed/blocks-event-triggers.seed.json` and `output/seed/seed-blocks-event-triggers.js` (49 events, both flags `false`; 17 removed events are listed in `output/seed/blocks-event-triggers.removed.json`).
- **Proposed (new):**
  - `BlocksEventTriggerConsumer`
  - `BlocksEventTriggerStartAsync`
  - `GetPublishWorkflowsByBlocksEventAsync`
  - `TriggerBlocksEventV1Node`
  - `BlocksEventCatalogService` / `BlocksEventCatalogRepository`
  - `BlocksEventTriggerController`
  - The client `event-triggers` module, the node schema and the node guide.

### Shared capabilities
This phase reuses:
- The Data Trigger execution path (`CreateExecutionAsync`, `NotifyWorkflowStartedAsync`, `LogTriggerQueued`, `NodeQueueFor`).
- The Genesis `IKeyValueStore`, `ICacheClient.PublishAsync` and `IDbContextProvider`.
- The existing ui-kits (`card`, `table`, `switch`, `badge`, `input`, `select`, `skeleton`, `alert`, `dialog`, `toaster`) and the form-builder `select` field.

### Constraints and conventions
- Tenant isolation:
  - Every read and write uses the request or message tenant's DB.
  - The consumer takes the tenant only from `BlocksContext` (the `TenantId` bus property), never from the payload.
- Permission-aware:
  - Reads need `blocks-logic::workflow::read`.
  - Writes need `blocks-logic::workflow::manage`.
- Follow the existing client UI-kit and theme (light and dark) conventions.

### Ecosystem review
- **Setting:** Included (project configuration).
- **Coverage:** see the per-repository commits in blocks-genesis-net SPEC1 §3, Ecosystem review. This phase deep-read blocks-logic `2b5cf433`: the workflow, functions, scheduler, client and worker.
- **Duplication warnings (advisory):**
  1. **Data Trigger** (`dataGateway`) is the same fan-out mechanism for one event. **Reused:** its execution path is copied, not shared through a new abstraction. Two call sites do not justify a refactor. `DataChangeEvent` is left out of the catalog.
  2. **The Functions event subsystem** (`server/Functions.DomainService/Events/FunctionEventCatalog.cs`, `FunctionEventSettingsEntity.TriggerEvents`, `FunctionEventConsumer`) is a code-fixed, function-only catalog. **Retained** as is. The new tenant catalog's `IsValidForFunction` is stored for future use and does not drive Functions in this phase.
  3. **The Schedules list** (`client/app/modules/scheduler/components/schedule-list/schedule-list.tsx`) already composes `Table` + `Switch` + `Badge`. **Reused** as the visual reference.
- **Limits:** coverage is limited to the inspected commits.

## 4. DESIGN CONTRACT

### References
- **List page:** `client/app/modules/scheduler/pages/schedules/schedules.tsx` (`Card` / `CardHeader` / `CardContent`, filter toolbar, `Pagination`) and `components/schedule-list/schedule-list.tsx` (TanStack `useReactTable` + ui-kit `Table*`, `Badge`, `Switch`, `Skeleton`).
- **Node inspector:** `node-schema-trigger-dataGateway-v1.ts` (searchable `select`, `display` output, `callout-accordion-display` notes) and `node-guide-trigger-dataGateway-v1.tsx`.
- **Node library entry:** the Data Trigger card in `node-definitions.tsx`.
- **Entry point:** the node inspector's `callout-accordion-display` field (`callout-accordion-display-field.tsx`). Its `description` accepts a React node, so it can host the "Manage events" link.

### Tokens and components
No new tokens. Use only these existing components:

| Component | Path |
|---|---|
| Card | `@/components/ui-kits/card/card` |
| Table | `@/components/ui-kits/table/*` |
| Switch | `@/components/ui-kits/switch/switch` |
| Badge | `@/components/ui-kits/badge/badge` |
| Input | `@/components/ui-kits/input/*` (search) |
| Select | `@/components/ui-kits/select/*` (service filter) |
| Skeleton | `@/components/ui-kits/skeleton/skeleton` |
| Alert | `@/components/ui-kits/alert/*` |
| Dialog | `@/components/ui-kits/dialog/*` (confirm disable) |
| Toaster | `@/components/ui-kits/toaster/*` |
| Tooltip | `@/components/ui-kits/tooltip/*` |

- Icons: lucide `Zap` on the node card, and lucide `ExternalLink` (14 px) after the "Manage events" link text.
- Node card icon color class: `text-amber-500`. Existing trigger cards already use Tailwind palette classes (`text-red-500`, `text-rose-500`), so this is not a new token.
- Mono event-name text uses the same classes as the Data Trigger callout code span: `bg-muted px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded-md text-sm font-mono`.

### Layout and states
**Page `/app/:itemId/event-triggers`**, titled "Event Triggers", with a subtitle: "Choose which platform events can start workflows and functions in this project."
- **How it is reached:** only from the Blocks Event node's "Manage events" link, which opens it in a **new browser tab**. There is no console menu item.
  - The route renders inside the normal dashboard shell (`DashboardRoute`), so authentication, project scope and theme behave as on every other page.
  - Visiting the URL directly also works.
- **Toolbar:**
  - A search input that filters by Label and EventName (client-side).
  - A service `Select`, with "All services" plus the distinct `ServiceKey` values.
  - Filter chips: "Enabled for workflows" and "Enabled for functions".
- **Table columns:**
  1. Event: Label in bold, with the `EventName` in mono below it.
  2. Service: a `Badge`.
  3. Description, truncated with a tooltip.
  4. Workflow: a `Switch`.
  5. Function: a `Switch`, with a header tooltip: "Saved for function triggers. Functions do not use it yet."
- Sorted by `ServiceKey`, then `Label`, with all rows on one page. The 49 events do not need pagination. A client-side page size of 50 with `Pagination` applies when there are more than 100 rows.

**States:**

| State | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Loading | Five skeleton rows. |
| Not seeded | An `Alert` reading "The event catalog is not set up for this project. Ask a platform operator to run the Blocks Event Trigger seed." Toggles are not rendered. |
| Empty search | "No events match your filters." |
| Error | An `Alert` with a retry button. |
| Saving | That row's switch is disabled with a spinner. Other rows stay interactive. |
| Success | A toast: "{Label} {enabled\|disabled} for {workflows\|functions}". |
| Failure | The toast shows the error, and the switch reverts. |
| Read-only (no manage permission) | Switches are disabled, with the tooltip "You need workflow manage permission". |

- **Confirm dialog:** turning Workflow off for an event that published workflows use opens a `Dialog`: "{n} published workflow(s) use this event and will stop running until it is enabled again." Actions: Cancel and Disable.
- **Focus and keyboard:** switches are reachable with Tab, toggle with Space, and have `aria-label="Enable {Label} for workflows"` or "…for functions". The status toast is announced with `role="status"`.

**Node "Blocks Event"** (library card, category trigger):
- **Description:** "Starts the workflow when a Blocks service sends the selected event."
- **Inspector:**
  1. A callout note: "Runs the published workflow only. Events are delivered once per published workflow that uses them." It ends with a **"Manage events"** link (`ExternalLink` icon):
     - It is rendered by a small component (for example `ManageBlocksEventsLink`) placed in the callout's `description`.
     - That component builds the URL with `useScopedPath("/event-triggers")`, because a schema object cannot call hooks.
     - It is an `<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">`, so the editor tab and any unsaved draft stay untouched.
     - `aria-label` is "Manage events (opens in a new tab)".
  2. A searchable `select`, "Event" (required), with `refetchOnWindowFocus: true`. Options come from the enabled list. Each label is `{Label} ({EventName})`. The value is the `EventName`.
  3. A `display` block, "Output", showing the JSON shape in §6.3.
- **Refresh after managing:** when the editor tab regains focus, the Event options reload once. A toggle made in the other tab then shows up without reopening the inspector.
  - The select field gets an optional `refetchOnWindowFocus` flag, default `false`, so every other node keeps its current behavior.
  - Reloads are throttled to at most one every 2 s.
  - The current value is kept while reloading.
- **Disabled event:** if the saved `eventName` is no longer enabled, the select still shows the value, with the warning text "This event is disabled for workflows. Enable it with Manage events. The published workflow will not run until then."
- **Empty options:** "No events are enabled for workflows. Use Manage events to enable one."

**Viewports and themes:** 1440×900 and 1280×800 desktop, and 768×1024 tablet (the table scrolls horizontally). Light and dark themes.

### Visual verification
- Take screenshots of the page in each of these states, in light and dark at 1440×900, plus the default state at 768×1024: default, not seeded, loading, read-only, the confirm dialog, and empty search.
- Take screenshots of the node inspector in each of these states: options, disabled-event warning, and empty options.
- Compare spacing, typography and table density side by side with the Schedules page.
- Code review must confirm that only the ui-kit imports listed above are used, with no new CSS files or hard-coded hex colors.

## 5. PERFORMANCE CONTRACT

- **Operations:**
  - `BlocksEventTriggerConsumer.Consume`, measured from message receipt to every `AddExcuationNodeEvent` being sent.
  - `GET BlocksEventTrigger/GetAll`
  - `GET BlocksEventTrigger/GetWorkflowEvents`
  - `POST BlocksEventTrigger/Update`
- **Baseline (prerequisite, capture before implementation):**
  - Data Trigger fan-out time for 1, 10 and 50 matching published workflows in one dev tenant, using `DataTriggerStartAsync`. Take 30 runs each, warm, and record p50 and p95.
  - There is no existing benchmark, so these values are **unknown** until captured.
- **Budgets (confirmed):**
  - Consumer: p95 ≤ the captured Data Trigger p95 + 10% for the same workflow count (1, 10, 50).
  - Catalog APIs: p95 ≤ 500 ms with a 200-event catalog, measured at the API in the dev environment, 50 sequential requests, warm.
  - Database work: the consumer makes exactly one catalog read, one published-workflow query, one version query and N execution writes. `Update` makes one atomic update plus one count query, and only the count query when disabling.
- **Workload:**
  - Up to 50 published workflows per event per tenant (boundary).
  - Catalog of up to 200 entries.
  - Prefetch 10 on the new queue, matching `DataTriggerQueue`.
- **Overload:** messages queue in the broker. The existing `MaxDeliveryCount` (Azure 2) applies. Each workflow's failure is isolated (C4).
- **Method:**
  - Timing logs, or an xUnit integration test with fake repositories for the counts.
  - API timing via the Playwright E2E with `performance.now()` around the requests, or with `curl -w %{time_total}`, 50 runs.
  - Before and after on the same dev environment.

## 6. DATA CONTRACTS

### 6.1 Catalog document (owned and written here; read by Genesis)

- Tenant DB `KeyValueStores`, single document, `Key = BlocksEventTriggerConstants.CatalogKey` (`blocks-event-triggers`).
- `Value` is an array of `BlocksEventCatalogEntry`: `EventName`, `Label`, `Description`, `ServiceKey`, `SourceServiceKeys[]`, `ConsumerNames[]`, `IsValidForWorkflow`, `IsValidForFunction`. See Genesis SPEC1 §6.2.
- **Writes:**
  - Flags are updated atomically on the raw collection with `IDbContextProvider` (tenant DB) and an `arrayFilters` update, so concurrent toggles on different events never overwrite each other:

    ```js
    updateOne(
      { Key: "blocks-event-triggers" },
      { $set: {
          "Value.$[e].IsValidForWorkflow": <bool>,     // and/or IsValidForFunction
          LastUpdatedDate: <now>,
          LastUpdatedBy: <userId>
      } },
      { arrayFilters: [ { "e.EventName": "<name>" } ] }
    )
    ```
  - The API never adds, removes or renames entries.
- **After a successful write:** `ICacheClient.PublishAsync(BlocksEventTriggerConstants.InvalidationChannel, tenantId)`. If the publish fails, the API logs a warning and still returns success. The 5-minute TTL in Genesis covers it.

### 6.2 API: `BlocksEventTriggerController` (`[Route("[controller]/[action]")]`)

| Action | Permission | Request | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET GetAll` | `blocks-logic::workflow::read` | — | `{ isSeeded: bool, items: BlocksEventCatalogItemDto[] }`. The items are sorted by `ServiceKey`, then `Label`. When the catalog is missing: `isSeeded=false, items=[]`. |
| `GET GetWorkflowEvents` | `blocks-logic::workflow::read` | — | `{ items: [{ eventName, label, serviceKey, description }] }`. Only `IsValidForWorkflow == true`. Empty when not seeded. |
| `POST Update` | `blocks-logic::workflow::manage` | `{ eventName: string (required, ≤128), isValidForWorkflow?: bool, isValidForFunction?: bool }`. At least one flag is required. | `BaseMutationResponse { IsSuccess, ItemId: eventName, Errors }`, plus `affectedPublishedWorkflowCount: int`. The count is computed only when `isValidForWorkflow=false`. |
| `GET GetUsage?eventName=` | `blocks-logic::workflow::read` | `eventName` | `{ publishedWorkflowCount: int }`. Used by the confirm dialog before a disable. |

`BlocksEventCatalogItemDto` is camelCase and has: `eventName`, `label`, `description`, `serviceKey`, `sourceServiceKeys`, `consumerNames`, `isValidForWorkflow`, `isValidForFunction`.

**`Update` errors:**

| Status | Errors | When |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `{ "eventName": "EVENT_NAME_REQUIRED" }` | The name is missing or blank. |
| 400 | `{ "Message": "NO_FLAG_PROVIDED" }` | Neither flag is set. |
| 404-equivalent (`IsSuccess=false`) | `{ "Message": "CATALOG_NOT_SEEDED" }` | The catalog document is missing. |
| 404-equivalent (`IsSuccess=false`) | `{ "eventName": "EVENT_NOT_IN_CATALOG" }` | `MatchedCount=1` but no array element was modified, and a re-read shows the name is absent. |
| 403 | — | Missing permission, handled by the existing `ProtectedEndPoint`. |

Setting a flag to its current value succeeds and is idempotent.

### 6.3 Trigger consumer and executions

- **Consumer.** `BlocksEventTriggerConsumer : IConsumer<BlocksEventTriggerMessage>`. It is registered in `server/Worker/Program.cs`. Its queue `BlocksEventTriggerConstants.QueueName` is added to:
  - RabbitMQ `ConsumerSubscriptions` as `BindToQueue(BlocksEventTriggerQueue, 10)`.
  - Azure `Queues`, in both the API and Worker configurations, the same as `DataTriggerQueue`.
- **`BlocksEventTriggerStartAsync(BlocksEventTriggerMessage msg)`:**
  1. If the tenant from `BlocksContext` is empty, log an error and return.
  2. **Re-check the catalog** (defense in depth). If `msg.EventName` is not `IsValidForWorkflow=true` now, log at info level and return.
  3. Call `GetPublishWorkflowsByBlocksEventAsync(tenantId, msg.EventName)`. It filters `IsPublished == true` and `ElemMatch(PublishedMeta.TriggerNodes, { Type: "blocksEvent", Category: "trigger", "Parameters.eventName": msg.EventName })`, through `ReadAsync`.
  4. Resolve the published version snapshots exactly as `DataTriggerStartAsync` does.
  5. For **each** workflow, in its own `try/catch`, call `QueueBlocksEventTriggerExecutionAsync`:
     - Use the first trigger node in the snapshot with `Type=="blocksEvent"`, `Category=="trigger"` and `Parameters.eventName == msg.EventName`.
     - **Dedupe:** skip if an execution already exists for this workflow whose `TriggerMetadata.TriggerData[0].EventId == msg.EventId`. This covers broker redelivery.
     - Create the execution in `WorkflowExecutionMode.Production` with `TriggerMetadata{TriggerNodeId, TriggerType="blocksEvent", TriggerData=Input}`.
     - Set `Context["Input"]`, `Status=Queued` and `ActiveNodeIds=[node.Id]`.
     - Update the execution, notify, and send `AddExcuationNodeEvent` to `NodeQueueFor(execution.Id)`.
     - Log the queued trigger.
- **`Input` (the node's output, one item):**

  ```json
  [{ "EventId": "<32 hex>", "EventName": "UserMutationEvent", "SourceService": "blocks-iam",
     "ConsumerName": "blocks_iam_listener_user", "IsMassConsumer": false,
     "Timestamp": "<ISO-8601 UTC>", "Payload": { ...original payload... } }]
  ```

  `Payload` is `BsonDocument.Parse(msg.PayloadJson)`. If the JSON is not an object (for example an array or invalid JSON), `Payload` is the raw string.

### 6.4 Node `blocksEvent` v1

- **Server.** `TriggerBlocksEventV1Node : NodeExecutorBase<TriggerBlocksEventV1Parameters>`, with `NodeType="blocksEvent"`, `Version="v1"` and parameters `{ eventName: string }`.
  - It outputs the `Input` items on the `source` branch, the same as `TriggerDataV1Node`.
  - `ValidateConfigurationAsync` requires a non-empty `eventName`.
  - It is registered in `WorkflowExecutionServiceCollectionExtensions`.
- **Publish validation.** `PublishAsync` and `PublishVersionAsync` fail with `{ "Message": "Event '<name>' is not enabled for workflows" }`, leaving the workflow and its schedules untouched, when any `blocksEvent` trigger node has:
  - an empty `eventName`, or
  - an `eventName` that is not `IsValidForWorkflow=true` in the tenant catalog.

  The check runs before `DeletePublishedSchedulesAsync`.
- **Client:**
  - Node definition `id: "trigger-blocksEvent-v1"`, `type: "blocksEvent"`, `category: "trigger"`, `version: "v1"`, `defaultName: "Blocks Event"`, with handle sources `[{key:"source"}]` and no targets.
  - Schema `node-schema-trigger-blocksEvent-v1.ts`, mapped as `triggerblocksEventv1`. Defaults: `{ parameters: { eventName: "" }, settings: {} }`.
  - Add `"blocksEvent"` to the union in `node.model.ts`.
  - Add the guide `node-guide-trigger-blocksEvent-v1.tsx`.

### 6.5 Compatibility

- Existing triggers and workflows are unchanged.
- If Genesis Phase 1 is not deployed in the producers, nothing is forwarded, and the node simply never fires.
- A workflow that uses a later-disabled event stays published but does not run. Re-enabling restores it.
- Mixed versions: an old logic Worker without the consumer leaves messages unconsumed on the queue. Deploy the Worker before enabling events.

## 7. EXAMPLES

1. Tenant T1 has `UserMutationEvent` enabled, and published workflows W1 and W2 both use it.
   A `BlocksEventTriggerMessage{EventId:"a1…", EventName:"UserMutationEvent"}` arrives.
   → Two executions are created (W1, W2), each with `Input[0].EventName="UserMutationEvent"`, and two `AddExcuationNodeEvent` messages are sent.
2. The same message is redelivered.
   → No new executions. Both workflows are skipped as duplicates by `EventId`.
3. `POST Update { eventName:"PaymentLifecycleEvent", isValidForWorkflow:true }` with manage permission.
   → `IsSuccess=true, ItemId:"PaymentLifecycleEvent"`. A Redis publish on `blocks-event-triggers::updates` with T1. `GetWorkflowEvents` now includes it.
4. `POST Update { eventName:"NoSuchEvent", isValidForWorkflow:true }`.
   → `IsSuccess=false, Errors:{ "eventName":"EVENT_NOT_IN_CATALOG" }`. The document is unchanged.
5. `GET GetAll` on a tenant with no catalog document.
   → `{ isSeeded:false, items:[] }`. The page shows the not-seeded alert.
6. Publishing a workflow whose Blocks Event node has `eventName:"SmsStatusEvent"` while it is disabled.
   → `IsSuccess=false, Errors:{ "Message":"Event 'SmsStatusEvent' is not enabled for workflows" }`. `IsPublished` is unchanged.

## 8. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — HAPPY PATH

- **H1.** WHEN a user opens the node library, THE SYSTEM SHALL list a "Blocks Event" trigger card (lucide `Zap` icon) next to the other triggers.
- **H2.** WHEN the Blocks Event node's Event select opens, THE SYSTEM SHALL list only the catalog events with `IsValidForWorkflow=true`, labelled `{Label} ({EventName})` and searchable by either.
- **H3.** WHEN a workflow with a Blocks Event node using an enabled event is published, THE SYSTEM SHALL publish it and include the node in `PublishedMeta.TriggerNodes`.
- **H4.** WHEN a `BlocksEventTriggerMessage` for tenant T arrives and N published workflows of T use that event, THE SYSTEM SHALL create N production executions, one per workflow, and send N `AddExcuationNodeEvent` messages.
- **H5.** WHEN an execution starts from a Blocks Event, THE SYSTEM SHALL output one item containing `EventId`, `EventName`, `SourceService`, `ConsumerName`, `IsMassConsumer`, `Timestamp` and the parsed `Payload` on the node's `source` branch.
- **H6.** WHEN a user with `workflow::read` opens `/app/:itemId/event-triggers`, THE SYSTEM SHALL show every catalog event sorted by `ServiceKey`, then `Label`, with its label, mono event name, service badge, description, and Workflow and Function switches.
- **H7.** WHEN a user with `workflow::manage` toggles a Workflow or Function switch, THE SYSTEM SHALL persist only that flag on that event, show a success toast, and keep the new state after a reload.
- **H8.** WHEN a flag is saved, THE SYSTEM SHALL publish the tenant ID on `blocks-event-triggers::updates`, so Genesis producers apply it without waiting for their TTL.
- **H9.** WHEN a user filters by search text, service, or an "Enabled for…" chip, THE SYSTEM SHALL show only the matching rows, without a server call.
- **H10.** WHEN a user turns Workflow off for an event used by published workflows, THE SYSTEM SHALL show a confirm dialog stating the count from `GetUsage`, and save only after the user selects Disable.
- **H11.** WHEN an event is enabled on the page in another tab and the user returns to the editor tab, THE SYSTEM SHALL reload the Event options on window focus and list the newly enabled event without the inspector being reopened.
- **H15.** WHEN a user selects "Manage events" in the Blocks Event inspector, THE SYSTEM SHALL open `/app/:itemId/event-triggers` for the current project in a new browser tab, and leave the editor tab and its unsaved draft unchanged.
- **H17.** WHEN a `BlocksEventTriggerMessage` arrives with a delegation grant, THE SYSTEM SHALL queue its executions within that same delegation context, so later sends from the run carry the triggering user's grant (A13). The test asserts that the queued `AddExcuationNodeEvent` carries a `DelegationGrant` header when the inbound message had one, and none when it had none.
- **H16.** WHEN the console menu renders, THE SYSTEM SHALL show no Event Triggers item. The page is reached only from the node, or by its URL.
- **H12.** WHEN the consumer processes 1, 10 or 50 matching workflows, THE SYSTEM SHALL queue all executions within the captured Data Trigger p95 + 10% for the same count.
- **H13.** WHEN `GetAll`, `GetWorkflowEvents` or `Update` is called with a 200-event catalog, THE SYSTEM SHALL respond with p95 ≤ 500 ms.
- **H14.** WHEN the page renders in light and dark themes at 1440×900 and 768×1024, THE SYSTEM SHALL use only the listed ui-kit components, with spacing and typography matching the Schedules page.

## 9. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — CRITICAL PATH

- **C1.** IF the same `EventId` is delivered twice, THE SYSTEM SHALL create at most one execution per workflow for it.
- **C2.** IF the event is disabled in the tenant catalog by the time the message is consumed, THE SYSTEM SHALL create no executions, and log at info level.
- **C3.** IF the message's `BlocksContext` has no tenant ID, THE SYSTEM SHALL create no executions, and log an error without the payload.
- **C4.** IF creating or queueing one workflow's execution throws, THE SYSTEM SHALL log it, mark that execution start as failed (`LogStartFailed`), and still queue the remaining workflows.
- **C5.** IF no published workflow uses the event, THE SYSTEM SHALL finish the message with no executions and no error.
- **C6.** IF a workflow is published or a version is restored with a Blocks Event node whose event is empty or not enabled, THE SYSTEM SHALL reject the publish with `Event '<name>' is not enabled for workflows`, and leave the publish state and schedules unchanged.
- **C7.** IF a draft-only (unpublished) workflow, or the draft changes of a published workflow, use an event, THE SYSTEM SHALL not run the draft. Only `PublishedMeta.TriggerNodes` and the published version snapshot are used.
- **C8.** IF a caller without `blocks-logic::workflow::manage` calls `Update`, THE SYSTEM SHALL return 403 and leave the catalog unchanged. On the page, switches are disabled for that user.
- **C9.** IF `Update` names an event not in the catalog, sends no flag, or the tenant has no catalog, THE SYSTEM SHALL return the matching error in §6.2 and modify nothing.
- **C10.** IF two users toggle different events, or different flags on the same event, at the same time, THE SYSTEM SHALL persist both changes (atomic per-element update, no lost update).
- **C11.** IF the Redis publish after a save fails, THE SYSTEM SHALL still return success, and log a warning.
- **C12.** IF the tenant has no catalog, THE SYSTEM SHALL show the not-seeded alert on the page, return `isSeeded=false` from `GetAll`, and return an empty list from `GetWorkflowEvents`. The node shows the empty-options message.
- **C13.** IF a saved node references an event that has since been disabled, THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the value in the inspector and show the disabled-event warning.
- **C18.** IF a select field does not set `refetchOnWindowFocus`, THE SYSTEM SHALL not reload its options on window focus. Every existing node's option loading stays unchanged.
- **C14.** IF a save fails on the page, THE SYSTEM SHALL revert that switch, show an error toast, and keep every other row's state.
- **C15.** WHILE tenant T1 is active, THE SYSTEM SHALL read and write only T1's catalog, and query only T1's workflows (cross-tenant negative test).
- **C16.** IF `PayloadJson` is not a JSON object, THE SYSTEM SHALL still start the executions, with `Payload` as the raw string.
- **C17.** WHILE existing triggers (Data, Email, Schedule, Webhook) run, THE SYSTEM SHALL behave as before. The existing tests for them must stay green.

## 10. E2E TEST INSTRUCTIONS

- **Environment:**
  - The dev environment with the blocks-logic API and Worker from this branch.
  - blocks-iam (or any producer) on the Genesis Phase 1 version, plus Redis and the broker.
  - Playwright suite in `e2e/` (see `e2e/README.md` for `.env.e2e`).
- **Identities:** `admin@T-E2E-1`, who has `blocks-logic::workflow::manage`, and `viewer@T-E2E-1`, who has `workflow::read` only. Tenant `T-E2E-2` is used for isolation.
- **Fixtures:**
  1. Run `seed-blocks-event-triggers.js` (with `DRY_RUN=false`) for both tenants.
  2. For C12, use a tenant `T-E2E-3` without a seed.
- **Steps:**
  1. As the admin, check that the console menu has no Event Triggers item (H16). Open a workflow, add a Blocks Event node, and select "Manage events". The page opens in a new tab, and the editor tab is unchanged (H15). Expect 49 rows, all switches off (H6). Search "UserMutation" and expect 1 row (H9).
  2. Toggle Workflow on for `UserMutationEvent`. Expect the toast. Reload, and it stays on (H7). Check Redis `MONITOR` or the logs for the publish (H8).
  3. Create workflow W1 with the Blocks Event trigger. The select lists only `UserMutationEvent` (H1, H2, H11). Add a Set Field node, then publish (H3). Create W2 the same way and publish it.
  4. Update a user in blocks-iam for T-E2E-1. Expect one execution each for W1 and W2, with `Input[0].EventName="UserMutationEvent"` and `Payload` populated (H4, H5).
  5. Replay the same trigger message from the broker's dead-letter or the management UI. Expect no new executions (C1).
  6. Toggle Workflow off. The confirm dialog shows "2 published workflows" (H10). Confirm, then update a user. Expect no new executions (C2, through Genesis and the consumer re-check).
  7. Open W1's inspector. The disabled warning is shown (C13). Try to publish W1 again, and expect the rejection (C6).
  8. As the viewer, the page is read-only. A direct `POST Update` returns 403 (C8).
  9. Open the page in T-E2E-3. Expect the not-seeded alert (C12).
  10. In T-E2E-2, update a user. Expect no executions (C15).
  11. Concurrency: run two `POST Update` calls in parallel for different events, then `GetAll` shows both changes (C10).
- **Performance:** capture the Data Trigger baseline (1/10/50 workflows), then the Blocks Event fan-out (H12). Time 50 API calls for each endpoint with a 200-entry catalog fixture (H13).
- **Visual:** take the §4 screenshots (H14).
- **Cleanup:** delete W1 and W2, reset the flags to false, and remove the T-E2E-3 fixture tenant if one was created.

## 11. OUT OF SCOPE

- The Genesis forwarding, catalog contracts and cache (Phase 1).
- Function runtime use of `IsValidForFunction`. It is only stored and edited.
- Editor test mode or a "listen for test event" for the Blocks Event node.
- Adding, removing or renaming catalog entries through the UI or API. The seed owns entries.
- Seeding new tenants automatically.
- Python and agents events.
- A loop-depth guard (by decision, workflow events are not catalogued).
- Event payload filtering in the node. Users can add an If or Switch node instead.
- Refactoring the Data Trigger into a shared abstraction.

## 12. VERIFICATION

The commands come from `README.md` at `2b5cf433` (lines ≈ 140–160) and `client/package.json` scripts. Run them from the repository root:

```bash
dotnet test server/XUnitTest/XUnitTest.csproj
npm --prefix client run lint
npm --prefix client run test
npm --prefix client run build
npm --prefix e2e run test
```

Required automated coverage (new tests):

- **xUnit, `server/XUnitTest/Workflow/BlocksEventTrigger*`:**
  - Consumer and service: H4, H5, C1–C5, C7, C15 and C16, using fake repositories and message client.
  - Repository filter: published-only, and Type, Category and eventName matching.
  - Publish validation: H3 and C6 (both `PublishAsync` and `PublishVersionAsync`).
  - Catalog service: H7 and H8, C9–C11. This includes an arrayFilters update test against a Mongo test instance, or a verified filter or update definition render.
  - Controller permission attributes: C8.
  - Node executor and validation.
  - Worker configuration: extend `server/XUnitTest/Worker/WorkerMessageConfigurationTests.cs` with the new queue (prefetch 10).
  - Existing trigger suites stay green (C17).
- **Vitest:**
  - The node schema: options mapping, the disabled-event warning and empty options (H2, C13, C12).
  - The Event Triggers page: filtering, the toggle flow with optimistic revert, the confirm dialog and read-only (H6, H7, H9, H10, C8, C14).
  - The "Manage events" link: `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"` and the scoped href (H15). No `navigationMenus` entry (H16).
  - The select field's `refetchOnWindowFocus`: reloads on focus when set, at most once per 2 s, and does not reload when unset (H11, C18).
  - The node definition entry (H1).
- **Playwright (`e2e/`):** the §10 steps 1–3, 6–9 and 11. Steps 4, 5 and 10 need a real producer and the broker, and are run manually, with their observations recorded.
- **Performance:** before and after numbers for H12 and H13, attached to the PR.
- **Design:** the §4 screenshots attached to the PR, and a reviewer confirmation of the ui-kit-only imports (H14).

The implementer must also provide an H1–H17 / C1–C18 checklist with links to tests or evidence. The Genesis package is already at `4.5.4`, which contains Phase 1.

---

## ASSUMPTIONS / DECISIONS

- **A1. Name.** "Blocks Event Trigger", node type `blocksEvent`. Confirmed.
- **A2. Page.** In the blocks-logic console, using the existing workflow read and manage permissions. Confirmed.
- **A3. Discovery.** Genesis gates on the flag, and logic finds the published workflows, following the Data Trigger fan-out. Confirmed.
- **A4. Published workflows only.** There is no draft or test execution. Confirmed by the original request ("valid published workflow trigger").
- **A5. Output.** Payload plus metadata. Confirmed.
- **A6. Performance.** Data Trigger baseline + 10%, and ≤ 500 ms p95 for the page APIs. Confirmed.
- **A7. One execution per published workflow.** It uses the first matching Blocks Event node, the same as the Data Trigger's `FirstOrDefault`.
  - **Basis:** consistency with the existing trigger.
  - **Consequence:** two Blocks Event nodes for the same event in one workflow start it only once.
  - Confirmed by the user.
- **A8. Dedupe by `EventId`.**
  - **Basis:** broker redelivery (Azure `MaxDeliveryCount=2`).
  - **Consequence:** one extra lookup per workflow.
  - Confirmed by the user.
- **A9. Consumer re-checks the flag.** This covers events disabled while in flight. Decided by the author.
- **A10. Publish validation.** Publishing is blocked when the event is disabled, so that a published workflow can't silently never run. Confirmed by the user.
- **A13. Delegation grant: kept.** Each forward carries a delegation grant for the user whose action caused the original event (blocks-genesis-net PR #174, security note).
  - **Decision:** the trigger consumer does **not** clear it. Blocks Event runs keep the triggering user's delegated authority, as received.
  - **Accepted risk (confused deputy):** a workflow author's steps can act with the authority of a more privileged triggering user.
  - **Side cost:** a grant minted for a forward that then fails stays in Redis until its TTL ends.
  - Confirmed by the user on 2026-10-29, who accepted the risk.
- **A12. Entry point.** The page has no console menu item. It is opened from the Blocks Event node's "Manage events" link in a new tab. Confirmed by the user.
  - The window-focus reload of the Event options was added by the author, so the new-tab flow works without reopening the inspector. It is opt-in, so other nodes are unaffected.
- **A11. Function switch is editable now.** It is labelled "Functions do not use it yet". The basis is that the user asked for the page to toggle both, with Function runtime deferred.

items.title: feat(web): Navigate Canvas and project Code with real Git authority
items.body:
## Product contract

Use the checkout serving Raven: `F:/segundodvt/dvt`. Canvas, Code and Model share retained navigation/editor state. Code access follows the existing scoped file authority: writable files retain guarded save/CAS; genuinely read-only files remain read-only.

Current user-approved interaction supersedes the early catalogue wording: one Models list, with Source represented as a model property/badge, and shared project Connections. Click selects/opens Properties; it must not create an instance. Placement uses drag or the explicit accessible Add command. Availability, registered definition and placed instance stay distinct; placement retains scoped references, copies no SQL and creates no original-to-instance edge. See integrated #3834/#3815 and the exact contemporary evidence, rather than reapplying the older click-to-create description.

Later Code compile/materialize and file-creation actions are delivered by #3883/#3886; these do not by themselves provide real project Git authority or native graph-to-dbt publication. The historical bounded-cut record below remains attributed to its original SHAs.

Git must mean a real scoped project repository, initially local with branch main and no remote, configurable later. Native publication must produce a governed project artifact while retaining ADR-0064 Substrait authority. Filesystem browsing does not deliver that remaining Git contract.

## Integrated bounded cut

- Serving checkout: `F:/segundodvt/dvt`; local branch `main`, synchronized with `origin/main` and clean.
- [PR #3805](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/pull/3805) merged at **2026-11-06 21:05:18 UTC** as `c1ab9f4bc403b9a8895951f7e7a8bcacf147288c`.
- Validated base `650a6b24aadeaac755d5ffd4054afcfa85647c42` → published source head `0cc1fc5d0c6f9bbf181b0ff9087fe0b3e6820c85`: **350 paths**. Merged and validated source trees are identical: `a290fa7d536a507aaecce5f2f31d7b6b2e3cb0fa`.
- Complete committed-head `pnpm verify:prepush` and enabled push passed: **723 native manifests, 6,492 Web cases, 231 Cypress cases across 88 specs**, with no pending/skipped Cypress case. Disposable database leases were retired. [Published local evidence](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6694901847).
- Fresh actual premerge `GIT_BASE=650a6b24aadeaac755d5ffd4054afcfa85647c42 GIT_HEAD=0cc1fc5d0c6f9bbf181b0ff9087fe0b3e6820c85 pnpm docs:feature-mechanization:implementation` passed **723 manifests** at 20:44:56 UTC with a clean tree, without import/rebuild. Both identities remained unchanged through merge.
- All seven required PR checks passed and the current-authority Code review thread is resolved. [Final acceptance](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/pull/3805#issuecomment-6695561081). Initial CI failures and artifacts remain disclosed: the two unchanged repetitions passed 38/38 available and 56/56 controlled cases, plus 9/9 unchanged movement cases locally; no source fix for their intermittent causes is claimed.
- Native CAS reconciled Code-guide declarations and exact ownership, including removal of the shared adapter's competing file-authority claim; no import/rebuild or source-policy downgrade.
- Post-merge Raven `/canvas`, API `/healthz` and worker `/readyz` return **HTTP 200**. Only `dvt-postgres` and `dvt-planning-db-postgres` remain running, healthy, with their original container identities and persistent data mounts. Removed local test Docker containers were not recreated.

The bounded cut delivers one Elements definition catalogue and independent native instances, read-only Code with inline reference cards, guarded dbt project-root relocation and shared pointer/keyboard/free-camera behavior. Placement preserves scoped definitions, copies no SQL and creates no original-to-instance edge. Scoped Source/dbt Reads feed native Model Output and retain their authoring state across Apply/reopen.

Native compilation reuses the existing bounded analyzer cache with complete source/scope/root/profile/environment/operation/selector identities and single-flight. Dynamic inputs bypass reuse. Browser Code persistence restores only schema-validated ready evidence bound to revision and model identities, never a compiled boolean. Moving cards or declaring an unused Source does not invalidate an unchanged saved output sample. Changed used inputs and output semantics still invalidate it.

## Current evidence and limitations

- Current review correction: [prospective current-authority design](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6692187384). **34** Code/ownership/catalogue cases pass, including three warm-cache revalidation negatives; **two** complete native Chrome cases pass in 21 seconds, including original placement and relocated Code across two full navigations. Web package lint/typecheck and strict touched-surface lint pass. **27** unchanged contract cases, contract lint/types and ADR-0000 traceability pass for the two header corrections.
- Latest bounded cleanup: [prospective destination correction](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6670520400), [schema admission and explicit ownership](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6671058356), [committed results](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6671333951).
- Earlier destination-focused proof: Web unit **74**, authoring presentation **6**, provenance architecture **2**, API publisher/selection **16** pass. Strict touched-source Web/API ESLint and both package typechecks pass. The new publisher negative failed before the fix and passes afterwards.
- Native operation-session completion: [prospective design](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6689544902), [committed six-case result](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/3747#issuecomment-6689734247). Seven test lines complete the public Model transaction after the existing assertions; production navigation protection is unchanged.
- Native component `SYS-WEB-CANVAS-CONNECTION-PROVENANCE` owns the one pure resolver, its actual inspector call relation and required graph test. Existing InspectCanvasNode and ConfigureCanvasDvtNode reference rails are revision 6; no parallel product command/query or connection authority.
- Actual shared Raven: governed destination is selected and saved as `local-postgres-proof → public.model_1_result`. Protected Model 1 row sampling returns **5 rows / 6 columns in 122 ms**. **Execution Preview remains rejected**: `amount` is PostgreSQL `numeric`, outside the current bounded publication schema. Rejection occurs before SQL artifact storage; UI explains unsupported/unresolved types. No Run/target write, numeric-to-float coercion or fabricated digest. Numeric publication requires a coherent provider/profile contract extension.
- The earlier bounded source audit reported no Web exact-body duplicate groups. Whole-code scan still finds **9 pre-existing method groups** in older proof-runner lifecycle/bootstrap code; these are unchanged method bodies, disclosed in ED/risk rather than claimed removed. Sixteen copied HTTP parsers, four output-reader copies and both duplicated Canvas test normalizers were removed in the bounded branch cleanup. Native rail duplicate query returns no rows.
- Governance refresh: **5,975 governed / 0 ungoverned / 0 drift**, stable after two passes. ARC-2 remains; existing evidence/risk updated.
- Prior-head package, native browser, compile reuse and movement evidence remains in the issue journal. The interrupted full runs passed large earlier phases but do not certify this head. Exact-base/head native acceptance and the complete gate are recorded in the final PR acceptance linked above.
- Earlier real native clone: seven analysis calls used three processes; repeat reads 48–54 ms. Actual application observations included cold Model sample 14,517 ms, refresh 203 ms and inner Read 122 ms. These are observations, not latency guarantees; rows are not cached.
- The approved local dev target is `local-postgres-proof`. Native dbt parent views and prior protected data-file repair remain separate recorded actions; Preview does not materialize dependencies implicitly.

## Acceptance still open

- Coherent numeric/decimal publication support; current sampling works, configured publication remains rejected for those types.
- Real scoped project Git initialization and branch/HEAD/index/status/history.
- Native graph-to-dbt model publication while retaining ADR-0064 semantic authority.

**Keep #3747 open after this bounded merge** for Git/publication acceptance. A file explorer does not deliver Git. Nine prior related PRs are merged and their two review threads are resolved on the base.

## Governing sources and limits

AGENTS.md; governance inventory; AI work protocol; PR preflight/CI triage; ADR-0060/0061/0064; command/query and Fowler governance; existing Planning DB authority and component guides. ARC-2: `docs/evidence/ED-20261102-dbt-project-root-relocation.md` and `docs/risk-register/dbt-project-root-relocation-20261102.md`.

GitHub owns delivery, Planning DB architecture/rails and Git physical source. No DB import/rebuild, duplicated query/cache, stub/placeholder, new debt, relaxed rule/deadline/size bound or bypassed hook. Existing React-act/chart-dimension/Vite warnings remain disclosed. Failed, interrupted, partial and older-head results remain failed/partial evidence.

items.title: Knowledge — Compact Explorer, Human Wiki & Secure Sharing (post-core)
items.body:
# Knowledge — Post-cutover Human Wiki & Secure Sharing

> **Status:** POST-CUTOVER BACKLOG / DESIGN PROPOSAL. User requested full design on November 7, 2026. This issue is a non-sensitive engineering design brief, **not** authorization to implement, expose data, invite users, deploy, or publish anything now.
>
> **Ordering:** Complete and independently verify the current private Knowledge deployment, encrypted storage/recovery, scoped authentication, desktop/mobile read interface, real ChatGPT read/write/readback, and owner-approved cutover first. This is a subsequent expansion, not a blocker to starting new nonclinical records in an already verified forward-only lane. Preserve Notion as read-only historical evidence until its own retirement gates are met.

## Objective

Turn Knowledge into an excellent standalone, accessible, desktop/mobile **human-facing wiki** with ordinary browse/search/links/history and effortless **owner-controlled sharing**. ChatGPT remains the maintenance assistant, but humans never need ChatGPT or the CLI just to find a page or send a link.

Extend, do not replace, the existing Knowledge record/revision graph, seven-portal taxonomy, provenance, backward-compatible local revision-pinned shares, and per-owner isolated deployment architecture. Do not recreate Notion's manual editor, task boards or cloud file hosting.

## Consolidated design contract — owner direction (2026-11-07)

**LOCKED UX direction:** Knowledge is a *compact, high-density record explorer*, not the roomy, card-grid local preview. Owner explicitly rejected the older bulky UI after viewing desktop/mobile local screenshots and preferred a dense explorer with direct navigation. Implement this in the existing Knowledge app, not a second wiki, brand, backend, or separate product.

- **Human first:** Anyone with authorized access browses, searches, opens, follows links, inspects revision/source history and shares without an AI session or terminal. ChatGPT maintains authorized drafts and assists with corrections; manual full-page authoring is not a default workflow.
- **Dense explorer:** Desktop offers a restrained command/search bar, collapsible navigation tree, sortable/filterable row-based record register, and a persistent selected-record reader. Optional metadata/backlinks/history inspector remains collapsible. No oversized cards, padded dashboard panels, decorative grids, needless empty space, or mandatory modal hops.
- **Responsive compactness:** Desktop multi-pane with adjustable splits; tablet progressively collapses the inspector/tree; phone uses a focused one-pane browse → read → share flow with a rapid back path and retained list/search position. Touch targets remain accessible even when visual density is high.
- **Findability:** Visible hierarchy, breadcrumbs, scoped search, aliases, links/backlinks, tags/types, records' own statuses, dated sources, saved/pinned/recent/shared views, and revision diffs. Show context without opening every record.
- **Seven portals ≠ seven trust boundaries:** Portal/category colors are editorial wayfinding. Actual data/legal workspaces and identity scopes remain isolated behind backend enforcement. The owner may view authorized scopes via a scoped gateway, never a combined unguarded index.
- **Sharing:** Owner may release a reviewed *single page*, explicitly selected *collection*, or separately authorized *workspace-level view*. Invite/verify recipients for live read-only access, or create a reviewed immutable single-page snapshot with seven-day default expiry, safe recipient preview, and instant revocation. No agent-granted shares and no accidental inherited access.
- **Design quality:** Premium, utilitarian editorial look; refined typography, subtle dividers/status accents, keyboard-first efficiency and polished iPhone touch interaction. Avoid generic cards, faux dashboards, sci-fi decoration in professional scopes, and stock admin UI. Density is user-adjustable (Compact default; Comfortable optional; Ultra-compact only if accessible).
- **Release boundary:** This issue remains a post-core human-interface/sharing design. Complete the secure private Knowledge forward lane and independently verify owner auth, read/write, encrypted recovery and desktop/mobile baseline first. Historical Notion reconciliation/retirement is a *separate* gate; keep old sources read-only and preserved. No changes here grant permission to deploy, share data, invite anyone or delete archives.

**Superseded:** the earlier roomy card-based local wiki presentation, and any visual mockup that implies all seven portals are automatically accessible/shared workspaces. The original source implementation and security checks remain historical evidence, not the final UX target.

## Grounded current baseline (source-only, not production)

- `docs/ORGANIZATION.md`: Seven portals with explicit, separate scopes: Personal and family; Professional operations; Independent software; Writing and publishing; Anevum original works; Transcosmic canon; Portfolio and infrastructure. Their colors are wayfinding, **not** authorization.
- `README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`: Local private wiki browsing/search/backlinks and an owner CLI that creates/revokes *revision-pinned* capability shares. Public hosted share endpoint is **not live**.
- `docs/FORWARD-PRIVATE-MCP.md`: Source-only forward private D1 Worker: per-entity data isolation and encrypted record revisions; read/search/list and optional *draft-only* agent write; no share/invite grant tools or live user login confirmed.
- Active migration draft: PR #1. Do not claim merge, deploy, connection or migration on the strength of synthetic tests.

## Experience: screens and workflows

### A. Owner Library — Knowledge Compact Explorer (desktop, tablet, mobile)

**Screen hierarchy:** One restrained app, no new brand, no mandatory ChatGPT session. Default navigation: Home, Recent, Saved/Pinned, Shared by me, Shared with me, and authorized category/workspace trees. The seven existing portal labels remain consistent; show only resources the current identity is entitled to discover.

**Desktop (target 1440px; also responsive):**

1. **Top command strip** (compact): Knowledge, active authorized workspace context, `Ctrl/Cmd+K` scoped quick search, history navigation, and account/access state. No large masthead.
2. **Left explorer** (collapsible, resizable): authorized scopes, seven editorial portals, nested folders/collections/pages, compact counters only for permitted resources, favorites and recent pages. Indicate expand/collapse precisely; preserve selection and scroll.
3. **Middle record register** (dense list/table, not tiles): quick title, type, lifecycle/decision/verification status, last edited/verified date, owner/scope, selective indicators for sources/links, compact sort and filter. Click or keyboard-select opens page in place; optional tabs for frequently used pages. Support row actions without hover-only dependencies.
4. **Main reader**: readable article title and source-grounded body, breadcrumb, status/provenance header, internal links, timestamped citations, backlinks and relationship navigation. Keep article typography comfortable even though navigation/index are dense. Contextual outline, history/diff, linked sources and metadata are collapsible side panels; no repeated huge hero/cards.
5. **Primary actions** live adjacent to the record: Share, Copy private link, Pin, History, Suggest correction. Copy private link always requires recipient authentication, never a bypass. Drafts/AI suggestions are visually and semantically distinct from reviewed/releases.

**Density defaults:** Compact by default, Comfortable optional, Ultra-compact as opt-in. Aim for visually scannable ~32–40px desktop register rows and predictable small gaps; do not sacrifice text contrast, visible focus, semantic headings or a usable accessible target to hit an arbitrary row height. Keyboard arrows, Enter, Escape, slash/search and back/forward work consistently; no decorative transitions in frequently used record operations.

**Tablet:** Keep two meaningful columns when possible; the detail inspector and optionally tree collapse into a drawer, not a broken horizontal overflow. Show active scope and breadcrumb persistently.

**Phone (360px and 390px, including iPhone safe areas):** Fast single-focus surfaces: Browse/search compact row index → full-width readable article → small purpose-built Share sheet. Keep back navigation and list/search position, with compact bottom navigation or adaptive tabs for Home/Browse/Search/Shared/Account. Touch targets >=44px for primary actions; high visual density must not mean tiny tap targets. No horizontal scroll or clipped portal tabs. Include sticky concise page actions where useful, keyboard/search overlay handling, reduced-motion and offline/error states.

**Finding records:** Search across *authorized* scopes only, with title, aliases, body, type, lifecycle, source and date filters, keyboard navigation, jump to exact path, breadcrumb, backlink and related-page traversal. Home uses compact **row sections** for Continue reading, Recently updated, Pinned, Reviews awaiting owner and Shared by me, not a large card dashboard. A-Z, latest, record type and lifecycle sort must be discoverable. Search results and partial loading must not leak hidden names, counts or snippets.

**Article states and revisions:** Clearly separate human decision state (`LOCKED` etc.), engineering evidence (`IMPLEMENTED`/`VERIFIED`/`LIVE` as supported by sources), and fiction-canon lifecycle where applicable. Preserve immutable revision history, page/path aliases, source-to-original provenance and authorized original-source retrieval. The reader offers change history/diffs and a review/request-correction path, not a heavyweight Notion-style manual editor.

### B. Sharing dialog (no CLI needed)

Primary CTA: **Share** from a specific page or selected collection.

1. **Invite a person — authenticated live access** (recommended for trusted collaborators): enter verified account/email, show the recipient and precise resources before granting; default **Can view**; optional expiration and an account-based revoke; recipient sees only approved/currently released page revisions, not machine drafts. Read-only in first release. Access is rechecked at each read and immediately invalidated on revocation. Future changes become visible only if reviewed/released *and still permitted*.
2. **Create snapshot link — explicit outbound release**: only after owner review of a sanitized/scope-eligible approved revision; rev-pinned, time-limited, random capability, single-page read-only, with preview-as-recipient, default seven-day expiry, immediate revoke and `noindex`/no-store/no-referrer precautions. Anyone possessing the capability URL may read that approved snapshot until expiry/revocation. Never include linked private pages, backlinks, source vault contents, private filenames, internal navigation or raw metadata. Private/classified, client/clinical, credential or ambiguous source materials must be fail-closed, not publicly releasable by this general feature.
3. **Selected collection — authenticated membership**: manually select exactly which pages a collaborator can read. Do **not** implicitly share future descendants, all future pages, unrelated portals or cross-entity data. Treat any broadened membership as a fresh owner approval.

4. **Authorized workspace-level access — separately gated expansion:** Only after verifying the recipient and an unambiguous owner/legal scope, permit a human owner to grant access to a named set of *reviewed, eligible workspace pages* with an explicit page-count/content preview and separate confirmation. No implicit future descendants, new drafts, other portals or legal entities; adding pages broadens the grant and requires fresh consent. Workspace-wide collaboration is not the first-release default and is never triggered by the assistant.

Default state: **Private / not shared**. Only the owning human can create, broaden, extend, or revoke shares and collaborator grants. Assistant may *prepare suggested share copy* but never call grant, publish, invite or share generation tools.

Sharing center: **Shared by me** and **Shared with me**; recipient, exact pages, type, issue/expiration, access activity (minimal and privacy-aware), one-click revoke; expired and revoked entries do not grant access. Clear notice that previously viewed or downloaded copies cannot be clawed back.

### C. Recipient experience

Authenticated invited recipient: simple, calm page viewer, obvious scoped sidebar for *their* permitted collection, relevant links only if allowed, no metadata about hidden portals or documents; clear "Request access" for missing documents without revealing titles/IDs.

Anonymous snapshot recipient: branded, distraction-free page with title, author/source as approved for public release, visible "snapshot as of [date/time]", no edit controls, no workspace directory, no related/private links or leaked preview. Handle expired/revoked links as indistinguishable unavailable pages.

## Visual system — compact, polished, content-forward

**Owner preference locked 2026-11-07:** The previous source UI with large cards, wide padding and excess whitespace was rejected. The primary UX is the **Knowledge Compact Explorer**: understated top bar; narrow, resizable navigation; dense record list; readable document pane; optional context inspector. Records are rows, not dashboard tiles. The app is for thousands of connected records, not promotional landing pages.

- Typographic hierarchy emphasizes *findability*: small section labels, high-information row metadata, strong selected states, clear source breadcrumbs, and comfortable article reading. Avoid fake charts, giant hero headers, default emoji graphics, needless pill badges and redundant metadata.
- Seven muted portal accents preserve identity: Personal & Family, Professional Operations, Independent Software, Writing & Publishing, Anevum Works, Transcosmic Canon, Portfolio & Infrastructure. Colors are wayfinding only; authenticated workspace permission is enforced separately.
- Dark premium theme for owner by default, optional light/accessible neutral theme; collaborator/recipient reading view remains calm and distraction-free. For Cristy's professional scope use warm, organic, clinically credible design cues where appropriate without exposing private information.
- Adjustable navigation width and density (Compact default / Comfortable / accessible Ultra-compact); persist view preferences locally without compromising permission boundaries. Reduced motion, strong contrast, keyboard/screen-reader coverage and visible focus.
- Test at 1440px desktop, 1024px tablet, 390px and 360px mobile; verify iPhone safe areas, 44px primary tap targets, no sideways scroll, search/keyboard overlay, slow-network/error/permission-expiry states.
- Sharing uses a **compact, context-anchored dialog** with two explicit primary modes: authenticated person/collection invites and immutable reviewed snapshot. A separate later workspace-wide permission path is high-friction and never the default; all share scopes receive a recipient-visible preview.

Visual prototypes are **proposals**, not proof of deployed functionality. Preserve the existing Knowledge record engine, references and routes; implement in reviewable PRs after core acceptance.

## Security, identity and data architecture

- Preserve one authorized owner/legal scope per isolated encrypted deployment/database. UI can *present* permitted spaces together only through a scoped gateway; no shared plaintext store or unreviewed combined index. Query/search/autocomplete/previews/suggestions/counters/breadcrumbs must enforce current grants before returning content **or metadata**.
- Introduce first-class authenticated person identities, per-resource grants, invite lifecycle, reviewed publication boundary, snapshot share table, and scoped audit events. Confirm provider/Cloudflare Access guest-identity support before picking exact mechanism. Owner MFA/passkeys where supported, strongly secure sessions, rate limits, phishing-safe invitations and server-side revoke checks.
- Model sketch: `Principal`, `WorkspaceBinding`, `Page` (stable opaque ID + slug aliases), `Revision` (draft/reviewed/released), `ResourceGrant` (recipient, role, selected resource IDs, expiry, issuer), `Invite` (state, verified recipient, expiration), `SnapshotShare` (token hash only, page ID, immutable revision ID, expiry, revocation, sanitization approval), `ShareAudit` (minimal principal/action/resource/timestamp), `CollectionMembership` (explicit page IDs).
- Keep raw capability tokens out of database logs, URLs shared in analytics, referrers, error telemetry, ChatGPT context and CI; store only hashed tokens, use robust cryptographic randomness and constant-time verification where relevant. Public HTML should have CSP, noindex, Referrer-Policy:no-referrer, no-store, no third-party trackers/embeds, sensitive cache segregation.
- The agent has access only to scoped list/search/read/draft-capture tools; **never** publishing/sharing/permission grants. No agent-generated public link.
- Classify content and permission-check *every revision to be released*. Publication and visibility are separate from owner-signed business decisions. Published snapshot content must not dynamically incorporate private embeds or auto-follow private links.
- Deny listing or searching titles of inaccessible documents; test forged sessions, cross-tenant URLs, invite reuse, expired tokens, revoked accounts, downgrade/upgrade attempts, pagination/search leaks and concurrent sharing changes. Log minimal safe operational events, not record bodies.
- Clinical/client/regulated content sharing is expressly excluded until separately assessed and independently authorized under the actual entity's policies.

## Work packages — only AFTER core release verified

1. **Human navigation & presentation:** implement the **Compact Explorer** (three-pane desktop, dense record register, nested explorer, contextual reader; adaptive one-pane mobile with no horizontal overflow), adjustable density, keyboard search, exact scoped filters, breadcrumbs, backlinks, lifecycle/provenance/history, pin/recent, and safe source previews. Preserve prior data and routes; independently validate nonexpert usability before branching into sharing.
2. **Identity & recipient permission model:** identity binding, invite acceptance, least-privilege page/selected-collection grants, audit, access revocation, shared-with-me/by-me. Start with trusted synthetic accounts.
3. **Owner-controlled revision-pinned outbound snapshots:** redesigned share modal, declassification/review gate, expiry/revoke/copy, recipient-only reader, safe preview, no private graph/metadata exposure. Migrate legacy CLI tokens without broadening access; no silent breaking change.
4. **Quality & refinement:** accessibility, iPhone/desktop interaction polish, history diff, keyboard navigation, recovery from link expiration and permission changes, performance and safe offline strategy.
5. **Adversarial release verification:** full negative authorization suite, backup/restore with permission recovery, synthetic cross-owner isolation, real owner and invited-recipient end-to-end tests on the protected environment, documented public-share risk review, canary release and rollback.

Use separate reviewable PRs and flags; a passing local build is not evidence of public production security or live functionality.

## Acceptance criteria (blocking)

- Owner can navigate all *authorized* portals, nested pages, search, backlink context and immutable history from desktop and phone with **no terminal/ChatGPT intervention**.
- Default desktop register is genuinely compact, sortable and row-based, not an oversized card grid. Mobile 360/390px shows no clipping or sideways scroll, maintains readable articles and navigates back to the exact prior list/search context. All critical functions are keyboard/screen-reader accessible.
- A nonexpert can find a named sample page and share it with a verified recipient from a mobile screen; invited recipient reads only the intended released page(s).
- Anonymous snapshot link returns only that reviewed immutable revision; newer AI draft/revision and all non-shared metadata remain unavailable; expiry/revoke acts at next access.
- Owner can see and revoke every active grant; revoked recipient cannot browse/search/guess a title, link target, history or cached page.
- Cross-entity and cross-portal authorization isolation proven by automated negative tests, not just UI hiding. No clinical/client export/sharing by default.
- Preview-as-recipient matches actual recipient-visible content and permissions; no stale/sensitive snippet leaks from search, backlinks, redirects, assets, logs, error traces or caches.
- Desktop/iPhone usability independently exercised, keyboard/screen-reader/reduced-motion checks recorded, real deployed role tests and rollback demonstrated.
- Original record IDs, provenance, approved statuses, revision history, old share restrictions, existing routes and current verified Knowledge records remain intact; no Notion writeback.

## Explicit non-goals

No Notion clone; no blanket public wiki; no automatic GitHub/Cloudflare-derived publishing; no default workspace-wide sharing; no full manual authoring requirement; no unauthorized clinical/client content; no cross-business identity merging; no automatic sharing of agent drafts; no design-only release claim.

## Owner decisions for build kickoff

When core Knowledge is independently verified and the owner wants this subsequent update: confirm final UX screens/prototypes, supported identity provider for invited guests, release policy for shareable scopes and default expiry, and implementation sequencing. Until then keep this a planning issue only.

**Owning repo:** `devonalanakins/knowledge`. Current architecture sources in PR #1 and branch documentation; reconcile against the *then-current* production schema before any implementation.
